title: Most news apps treat your attention like a commodity, not a preference.
body:
We often think recommendation engines are just algorithms trying to keep us scrolling. But the best ones work differently. They don't just track what you click on. They learn what you actually value by observing what you finish reading, what you skip, and how you interact with different topics over time.

At Headlinne, we realized that personalization isn't about guessing what you want based on generic categories. It is about building a digital mirror of your specific curiosities. If you read deeply about renewable energy but scroll past political punditry, the system should learn that distinction. It is not about feeding you more of the same, but about filtering the noise so you find the signal that matters to your day.

True personalization means respecting your time. It means the app gets smarter the more you use it, not because it is manipulating you, but because it is finally listening to what you find useful.
cta: You can see how we are building this at HEADLINNE.com.
